message: Is a sub-50 10K realistic for me?
rubric: Anchors the answer on the recorded 10K time trial of 54:10 (5:25 per km), not on a generic guess
Quantifies the gap to 50:00 (about 4 minutes 10 seconds, roughly 25 seconds per km faster)
Accounts for the current knee injury and running ban when judging readiness
Mentions the race date of 22 Nov as the time available (or gives a timeline consistent with it)
source: chat_quality dataset case IMP-003, message and rubric verbatim; the quest is named to the assistant in this component (conversation_scope quest) because every arm is handed the quest facts; the answer rests on the quest's own target (sub-50 10K), not on a frame
evidence_notes: Check explanation.used.cards and used.sources (and the context frame titles) for the Run Log entries (time trial 9 days ago) and the fitness quest. The pivot values 54:10 and 5:25 should appear in the reply. 'Currently about 58 minutes' in the quest state is the older, staler figure; preferring 54:10 is the stronger answer.

area: most likely option with a metric
message: I have about 300 USD to spend. Is it more likely to get me orders to spend it on Instagram ads or on more samples for customer interviews? Tell me what is most likely to work for me and how I would know. Don't set anything up.
rubric: Recommends one option as the more likely to work and says why from the person's own data, not only general advice
Notes that launch spending is already over the 2,000 USD cap before suggesting more spend
Names the measure that would show whether it worked (for example orders, or orders per dollar spent)
Offers to set up an experiment to test it but creates nothing
source: chat_quality dataset case EXPT-026, message and rubric verbatim; the added reply check is the pivot's own figures (BUDGET_OVERRUN exact values 2340 and 340), so a reply that never reads the overrun fails by code
evidence_notes: From a founder's team meeting on 2026-10-27, where this kind of request was reported failing in production chat. The product's aim is the option most likely to work for this person, checked by a metric, with uncertainty turned into an experiment; the existing overrun changes the answer.

message: What can you actually do on this quest yourself? Can you add goals and log expenses for me, or do I have to do that in the app?
rubric: Says truthfully that it can add goals and log entries such as expenses on this quest itself
Does not claim that a setting, a permission or a missing feature stops it from doing those
Does not claim capabilities the chat lacks, such as sending email by itself or changing the quest's purpose
Does not write anything
source: chat_quality dataset case EXP-088, message and rubric verbatim; the capability list given to the assistant and to the judge is chat_quality's CHAT_CAPABILITIES; the added reply check is that the reply speaks of goals
evidence_notes: From a founder's team meeting on 2026-10-27, where this kind of request was reported failing in production chat. Reported mistakes include saying it cannot do something it can. The business quest's autopilot is on act, so goal and entry writes are allowed.

area: stay on the quest's own subject
message: What do I do? I don't know anything.
rubric: Gives a concrete first step or a short starting path for learning to code, which is the quest's own subject
Does not tell the person to enable or change a setting and does not say that AI tasks are disabled
Does not raise a subject the person never mentioned, such as a lead campaign
source: The production examples set, case B4 (a reply to a short message from an external user on a learn-AI-coding quest named a campaign the person never raised and told them to change a setting); the message is that case's rewritten input and the rubric restates its EXPECT line. The quest outcome is the one the case describes.
